skill.name: security-quick-review
skill.description: Review code changes for secrets, injection, access control, unsafe operations, and dependency risks. Produce evidence-based triage before merging sensitive changes.
skill.summary: Triage code security risks with scoped findings, realistic impact, and specific fixes.
skill.author: agentkitco

The skill prohibits live exploitation and secret disclosure, while limiting review to scoped code and local tests. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential collection, or data exfiltration.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 20 uses Markdown backticks around git diff and git log -p for scoped history inspection. These are legitimate read-only review commands, not Ruby execution or injected shell input.
Line 25 lists eval and exec as unsafe operations to identify during review. The backticks format code names; no instruction executes either operation.
Lines 31 through 39 contain a fenced plain-text report template with scope, severity, fixes, and limitations. The fence is Markdown formatting, not an executable shell block.
Line 20 identifies private keys as secrets to detect and explicitly forbids repeating secret values in reports. No credential values, harvesting instructions, or external recipients appear.
Line 16 defines review scope and asks reviewers to inspect code called by the changed code. This is dependency-aware code review, not host reconnaissance or unauthorized system enumeration.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes for Security Risks
content.value_statement: Security defects can hide in small changes to input handling, authentication, and configuration. This skill guides scoped code triage with evidence, realistic severity, and actionable fixes.
actual_capabilities: Defines reviewed and excluded scope, including code called by a change.
Guides secret checks in source files, configuration, tests, logs, and scoped Git history without repeating secret values.
Checks untrusted input paths for injection, path traversal, SSRF, and authentication or authorization gaps.
Reviews data exposure, unsafe deserialization, TLS settings, randomness, and request size limits.
Examines dependency changes, lockfiles, configuration permissions, and failure behavior.
Structures findings by severity with file and line evidence, exploit sketches, specific fixes, and verification limits.
limitations: Provides AI-assisted triage, not a comprehensive security audit or penetration test.
Cannot verify runtime behavior, infrastructure settings, or inaccessible code from source review alone.
Does not supply a bundled scanner, vulnerability database, or automated dependency verification tool.
Requires human review for changes handling money, health information, or identity data.

use_cases.title: Review a Sensitive Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check authentication, input handling, and related call paths before merging a change.

use_cases.title: Triage Dependency and Configuration Changes
use_cases.description: Inspect package changes, lockfiles, CI permissions, and failure behavior within a defined release scope.

use_cases.title: Prepare Findings for Human Review
use_cases.description: Collect evidence, realistic impact, and verification gaps for a focused follow-up security assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this diff for likely security issues. State the scope, cite file and line evidence, and suggest specific fixes without revealing secrets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: an initial security pass over a small change.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [endpoint] and its called code for untrusted input, injection, authorization gaps, and data exposure. Separate verified findings from unresolved questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review a route and its related implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Release Diff
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [release diff] for secret exposure, dependency changes, configuration permissions, and failure behavior. Inspect scoped Git history without printing secret values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess multiple security-sensitive change categories.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Sensitive Data Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace authorization and data flow through [module] and its callers. Rank evidence-backed risks, propose local regression tests, and identify checks requiring human verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: examine cross-module assumptions around sensitive data.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: review a change that retrieves customer records by a supplied identifier.
output: Scope: the changed handler and its record lookup; deployed access policies were not reviewed.
Illustrative high-severity issue: missing ownership validation could expose another customer record.
Fix: constrain retrieval to the authenticated customer and add a local cross-account access test.
A real finding must include the reviewed file and line before this conclusion is accepted.
Limits: automated triage only; obtain human review for identity-sensitive changes.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: summarize a scoped review where no concrete issue was identified.
output: Scope: the supplied diff and available called code.
Checked, nothing found: secrets, injection, authorization, data exposure, unsafe operations, dependencies, and failure behavior.
Could not verify: deployed infrastructure permissions and runtime configuration.
Limits: no findings in the reviewed scope does not establish that the application is secure.

best_practices: Provide a clear diff or module scope and make relevant called code available.
Require file and line evidence, realistic impact, and a specific fix for every finding.
Keep secret values out of reports and rotate confirmed exposed credentials.
anti_patterns: Treating automated triage as proof of security or a substitute for a professional audit.
Testing exploit ideas against live systems during the review.
Publishing secret values or generic vulnerability lists without concrete code evidence.

faq.question: Is this a full security audit?
faq.answer: No. It guides fast AI-assisted triage and explicitly states that results are not a security audit or penetration test.

faq.question: What code should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a diff, directory, or endpoint and the relevant code it calls. Clearly identify anything outside the review scope.

faq.question: Does it execute attacks against production?
faq.answer: No. The instructions prohibit exploitation against live systems and permit code inspection and local tests.

faq.question: How are exposed secrets reported?
faq.answer: Reports identify the file and line without repeating secret values. Confirmed exposed credentials should be rotated, even after removal from code.

faq.question: Does it include a standalone security scanner?
faq.answer: No. The skill supplies review instructions and a report format, not a bundled scanner or vulnerability database.

faq.question: What does a clean result mean?
faq.answer: It means no issue was found in the reviewed scope. Runtime checks, infrastructure verification, and sensitive-domain human review may still be necessary.
